info.name: Laundo API v1
info.description:
# Laundo API — v1

Every endpoint under `/api/v1`, generated from `routes/api.php`.

## Getting started

1. Select the **Laundo — Local** environment (or edit `base_url` on this collection).
2. Run **04 · Auth — customer → Login**. The token is written to the `token` collection
   variable automatically, and every protected request inherits it.
3. For the driver folders, run **17 · Driver app — auth → Driver login**; that one fills
   `driver_token`.

Requests that create something (address, order, complaint, repeat schedule) save the new
id into a collection variable, so the later requests in that folder work without copying
ids by hand. The list endpoints for prompts, notifications and driver tasks do the same
with the first row they return.

## Headers

| Header | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Accept` | `application/json` | Required. |
| `lang` | `ar` \| `en` | Optional. Read by `ApiLocale`; falls back to the default language. |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <token>` | Protected routes. Sanctum personal access tokens. |

## The response envelope

Every response — success or failure — is shaped the same way, and the envelope `code`
always equals the HTTP status, so a client may branch on either.

```json
{
  "key": "success",
  "msg": "human readable, translated",
  "code": 200,
  "data": {},
  "errors": {},
  "meta": {}
}
```

`key` is one of `success`, `fail`, `not_auth`, `forbidden`, `not_found`,
`validation_error`, `throttled`, `server_error`. `errors` appears on validation failures
only; `meta` (`current_page`, `per_page`, `has_more`, `total`, `last_page`) on paginated
lists only.

## Rate limits

The whole group is throttled at **60 requests / minute** per user or IP. Four endpoints
carry a tighter limiter of their own, because requesting a code is cheap for us and
expensive in SMS while guessing one is cheap for an attacker:

- `throttle:otp` — register, resend OTP, forgot password (customer and driver)
- `throttle:otp-verify` — verify OTP, reset password (customer and driver)
- `throttle:login` — customer and driver login

## Conventions worth knowing

- **Status** fields are the strings `active` / `inactive`, not booleans.
- **Phone numbers** are Egyptian: `01[0125]XXXXXXXX`, optionally prefixed `+20`.
- **Translated text** is resolved server-side from the `lang` header; the API never
  returns the raw `{"en":…,"ar":…}` JSON.
- **File uploads** use `multipart/form-data` on **POST**, never PUT — PHP does not parse
  a multipart body on PUT.
- **Ownership** is enforced by scoping every lookup through the authenticated user, so a
  guessed id returns **404**, not 403.

exec: pm.test('Responds with the API envelope', function () {

header.description: ar | en — read by the ApiLocale middleware. Optional; falls back to the default language.

request.description:
The windows a customer may choose to be visited in.

**These are the platform's visiting windows, not a laundry's opening hours.** A laundry has no opening hours anywhere in this system. A slot is the three-hour window in which a *driver* comes to the customer, and the customer is the one who picks it - «02:00 مساءً – 05:00 مساءً» in the design.

Windows rather than exact times, because a driver on a route cannot promise 16:07. Five cover the day: 09-12, 12-15, 15-18, 18-21, 21-24.

| Parameter | In | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | query | `pickup` or `delivery`. Returns slots marked for that end plus every `both` slot. |

Each slot carries `applies_to` (`pickup` / `delivery` / `both`), and the order request enforces it - a delivery-only window cannot be sent as a pickup.

What a chosen slot actually does: it tells the customer when to expect somebody, and it sets `due_at` on that leg, which is the only thing «متأخرة» in the driver app means.

**Capacity is enforced.** Pass `date` and each slot comes back with `remaining` and `is_full`, so the wizard can grey out a full window instead of finding out at submit.

- A pickup and a delivery in the same window are two journeys to two doors, so both count.
- A cancelled order gives its place back.
- `remaining: null` means uncapped; `0` means choose another window. The app must draw those differently.
- Placing an order into a full window is a **422** on `pickup_slot_id`. Rescheduling into one is refused too. A confirmed repeat-schedule prompt is the one exemption — that screen has no slot picker to send the customer back to.

item.description:
Each endpoint carries its own rate limiter (defined in `AppServiceProvider`). They differ on purpose: requesting a code is cheap for us and expensive in SMS, while guessing one is cheap for an attacker.

Verification codes are **never** returned in a response, on any environment — read them from the log during development.

Creates the account and sends the first code. The account cannot sign in until the code is confirmed.

Throttle: `otp`. A phone already registered is refused, verified or not. Phone must match the Egyptian format `01[0125]XXXXXXXX` (a leading `+20` is accepted).

`referral_code` is optional and **never validated against the users table**: a mistyped code must not stop somebody registering, and confirming whether a code exists is a way to enumerate them. An unknown code is silently ignored. A valid one records the link - the coupons are issued later, when this customer pays for their first order.

item.name: 07 · Orders
item.description:
Isolation works as it does for addresses: every lookup starts from the authenticated user's own orders, so an id belonging to somebody else is a 404, not a leak.

Note this is a *customer* route group — the Order model's tenant scope is inactive here, because a customer is not a tenant.

exec: pm.test('Responds with the API envelope', function () {

header.description: ar | en — read by the ApiLocale middleware. Optional; falls back to the default language.

request.description:
The summary step's price preview, before anything is saved. Runs the same pricing pass as **Place order**, so the two cannot disagree.

Only what pricing actually depends on is required — scheduling and notes have no effect on the total.

A refused coupon is never fatal: `coupon_error` explains it and the quote still returns. `delivery_fee_reason` is non-null when the fee could not be worked out, so the app shows «يتم تحديدها لاحقاً» rather than a misleading 0.00.

`payment_method` belongs here because the cash surcharge depends on it and «شاشة اختيار الدفع» re-quotes as the customer picks.

`payment_method` accepts **`cash` | `card` | `wallet` | `instapay`**. It is read by pricing, not merely stored: choosing `cash` adds the configured `Cash_Surcharge` as its own line in the response (`cash_surcharge`), applied **after** any coupon - a coupon discounts the washing, not the cost of handling notes. Sending nothing returns a surcharge of 0, which is right for a quote taken before the customer has chosen how to pay.

`accepts_review_terms` is **required and must be truthy** — the whole of the review flow rests on it: the customer is agreeing that the price they just saw is an estimate and the real one arrives after the pieces are counted.

`items` may be an empty array for a quote-priced service costed after inspection; the service rejects an empty basket where it matters.

An absent `delivery_address_id` means «same address». `delivery_method` is `door` or `leave`.

To attach stain photos (max 5, jpg/jpeg/png/webp, 5 MB each) switch the body to **form-data** and send `photos[]`.

**Saves `data.id` into `order_id`.**

`payment_method` accepts **`cash` | `card` | `wallet` | `instapay`**. It is read by pricing, not merely stored: choosing `cash` adds the configured `Cash_Surcharge` as its own line in the response (`cash_surcharge`), applied **after** any coupon - a coupon discounts the washing, not the cost of handling notes. Sending nothing returns a surcharge of 0, which is right for a quote taken before the customer has chosen how to pay.

**Photos** - «أضف صوراً للبقع الصعبة» - are accepted here as up to 5 image files under `photos[]`. That needs a `multipart/form-data` body rather than the JSON above; duplicate the request and switch the body mode to form-data to try it.

request.description:
The tracking screen: the five-point timeline plus which steps have been reached and when.

`driver` is the card the design draws - «مندوب الاستلام · أحمد · ★ 4.9»:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `name`, `image` | Whoever holds the leg in flight; the last completed leg between journeys. |
| `role` | Which of the four legs - the person collecting and the person returning are usually not the same. |
| `rating` | The average of **delivery** ratings alone, never the wash. `null`, not `0`, until somebody has rated them. |
| `location` | `{lat, lng, updated_at}` - the live dot. |

`driver` is null before anybody is assigned. `driver.location` is null in three more cases, each deliberate: the leg does not end at the customer (the runs to and from the laundry are not broadcast), the driver has not reported yet, or the last reading is over two minutes old - a frozen marker reads as a driver who has stopped.

**No phone number.** Handing out a driver's personal mobile is a policy decision, not a field.

item.description:
«ما رأيك في تجربتك؟»

The GET is not symmetry: the design puts a «تقييم» button on a completed order in the list, and `can_rate` decides whether it is drawn at all — a button that opens a screen which then refuses is worse than no button.

header.description: ar | en — read by the ApiLocale middleware. Optional; falls back to the default language.

request.description:
`overall` (1–5) is required — the aspect scores are optional because «تخطي» exists, but a rating with no score is not a rating.
